report:
Reviewed the complete claim: (1) already published symbols remain usable during incomplete expansion; (2) missing symbols justify exhaustive negative answers only under a complete expansion; (3) completeness is relative to the semantic question, including unsupported functionality and resource bounds rather than scheduling progress. The initial mods.rs implementation plus seven newly associated essential helper files account for the implementation chain. mods.rs publishes ordinary items and represented macro/derive output, omits errors and active-attribute inputs, and computes completeness separately. bang_macro_expansion_complete rejects unresolved/ambiguous macros, active attributes, error output, and the 128-level bound. macro_invocations.rs converts expansion failure to an Error item. Trait completeness checks derive resolution and supported output; builtins.rs explicitly returns None for unsupported input forms and maps known derive traits hygienically so an unsupported different builtin need not block this specific trait question. Method-provider completeness accepts compiler builtins that cannot introduce providers, while symbol-listing completeness requires represented output and recursively checks children. These differing policies honor the semantic-question qualification.

local_syms/impls.rs recursively gathers usable impls without discarding their evidence when its separate completeness flag becomes false. clauses.rs propagates that flag into candidate assembly (and uses semantic orphan-impossibility for irrelevant local sources). prove.rs passes the flag to merge_candidate_results. merge.rs preserves an unconditional proven answer regardless of incomplete sources; empty/no successful candidates produce No only when the source is complete. Otherwise anti_unify.rs returns Maybe, including the unconstrained possibility from incomplete discovery. These associations were added so changes in essential source invalidate this review.

All five associated tests were inspected. unresolved_item_macro_prevents_ground_no and malformed_item_macro_output_prevents_ground_no_without_panicking visibly construct ground bool: Marker goals and assert Maybe for missing and malformed macro output. Newly associated no_candidates_is_no_only_for_complete_source visibly compares the same empty candidate set under complete and incomplete flags and asserts No versus Maybe. unconditional_yes_wins_over_incomplete_source supplies a proven unconditional answer and asserts Yes despite incompleteness; its yes helper constructs empty substitution and true modulo. Test setup helpers create a real local module/database and recover the local trait and crate, not mocked answers.

The fifth entry, sage_meta::todo::modules_expand_completeness, remains an explicit test TODO, not passing evidence. Its prerequisite is a complete source-to-ground-query verification matrix with visible per-scenario assertions for successful, unresolved, malformed, unsupported, and resource-limited expansions. Current ordinary tests cover unresolved/malformed input and merge polarity; they do not establish the entire semantic-question/unsupported/resource-bound matrix. The captured additional successful and recursive item-macro tests and their execution provide useful corroboration but retain helper-hidden assertions and are not substituted for complete annotated coverage. The explicit TODO accurately preserves that remaining verification work; no implementation obligation was reclassified as TODO.

Executed cargo fmt, cargo build (passed with existing warnings), cargo test -p sage-ir check::solve::merge::tests --lib (13 passed), and cargo test -p sage-test-harness item_macro --lib (6 passed, including the two associated macro regressions, successful expansion, failed expansion, recursive limit, and method-scope incompleteness). Fresh start after all association edits and captured helper reads support this report. This is source review plus those exact executions, not a claim of exhaustive testing. Coordinator owns centralized delegated post-codegen and Sage sanity checks for the comment/attribute-only Rust changes. No behavioral defect found and no requested edits; the documented test TODO remains deferred.
